text:
anya: FYI canary for model-serving:v2.3 started and is scheduling onto nodepool with label gpu=legacy in eu-west-1. We're seeing evictions and other tenants getting GPU pressure. Can we pause/rollback the canary?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for model-serving:v2.3 started (canary=10%). ArgoCD sync id: sync-2026-03-18-1023

sam: Any recent chart/values changes? I noticed a change in values.yaml (replicaCount + nodeSelector) in commit 815b3f4.

tariq: Confirmed — helm values accidentally set `nodeSelector: {gpu: \"legacy\"}` while testing a dev anchor. Should have been `gpu: \"main\"`.

jess: Metrics: eu-west GPU util jumped to ~95%. Cluster-autoscaler isn't adding nodes because the nodeSelector/taints don't match the large GPU pool. We need a quick rollback to reduce load.

matt: ArgoCD supports rollback/pause. I can abort the canary sync and revert to v2.2 canary. Who wants me to run `argocd app rollback`?

anya: Go ahead, rollback to v2.2 canary and remove the canary traffic. Also plan to drain pods from the small legacy pool.

matt: Running commands now:
```
argocd app rollback model-serving --revision v2.2
kubectl -n serving rollout status deploy/model-serving
```
I'll also toggle the rollout pause flag.

deploy-bot: Action queued: argocd rollback initiated by matt. Job id: 4521. ETA ~40s.

sam: In parallel, I'm preparing a terraform patch to fix the node pool label mapping. Draft patch:
```
resource \"google_container_node_pool\" \"gpu_legacy\" {
  node_config {
    labels = { gpu = \"legacy\" } # currently wrong
  }
}
# patch: set labels = { gpu = \"main\" }
```
Will run `terraform plan` then `apply` if safe.

tariq: Heads up: changing node pool labels can be destructive (some labels are immutable). Safer path is to patch the deployment's nodeSelector in git and let ArgoCD sync, or a temporary kubectl patch to immediately relieve pressure.

anya: Agree. Do the GitOps-safe path for the long term. For now, an emergency patch to the canary deployment is fine to buy time.

matt: Applying an emergency kubectl patch to the canary to point at `gpu: main` so it schedules onto the larger pool:
```
kubectl -n serving patch deploy model-serving-canary -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"gpu":"main"}}}}}'
```
Note: this is an emergency manual override; it will be reverted when the git sync runs.

jess: After rollback/patch, I'll watch for evictions and tail latency. Setting a temporary alert: node gpu util > 85% for 5m -> page oncall.

argo-bot: ArgoCD sync: model-serving reverted to v2.2 by matt at 2026-03-18T10:24:17Z. Sync successful.

anya: Thanks everyone. Action items for follow-up: 1) Add a lint rule to the PR template that checks nodeSelector values against an allowed map. 2) Add a pre-deploy canary gate that verifies the targeted node pool exists and has >= requested GPUs. 3) Document emergency rollback + kubectl patch steps in runbook.

tariq: I'll open the PR for the lint rule and add a preflight check in our GH action workflow.

sam: I'll investigate terraform drift and whether someone manually edited node labels.

matt: I'll keep the incident open until metrics are stable and then reassign to eng-platform for the follow-up tasks.

anya: Closing note: avoid infra changes during canaries unless validated by the preflight. :thumbsup:
